title: MoMoney
headline: I built the script and dashboard that put brand offers inside mobile games
summary: MoMoney lets a game studio add a small offers unit at a natural break, like a cleared level, where players see a few brand perks to claim or save.
description: At work I built MoMoney's hosted script, dashboard work, demos and default contracts, plus the offer units in one Android game.
outcome: My offer units shipped in an Android game on Google Play.

hero.alt: Left, a level-cleared screen with three stars and Main Menu and Next Level buttons. Right, an offer sheet for a free bag of coffee from an invented brand, with Claim and No thanks buttons and Ad and Terms labels.
hero.caption: The moment, then the unit: the shooter's level-cleared screen, and an offer sheet with an invented brand.

story: A cofounder started the product and a games engineer built both in-house games. I built the offer layer in the shooter, early features in the puzzle game, the hosted script, the dashboard work, the demos and the default contracts.
Before selling it, I proposed putting the product in our own puzzle game.

calls.why: Studios wouldn't hand-integrate an API just to try a format. So I built one script they paste in. It handles several formats and reports no-fill and error reasons back to the game.
I closed my own change that added a sponsored tag and a terms line. The advertiser's logo and name should lead each unit.
In the unit rebuild I started in November, close shows from the first frame, save never leaves the game, and an offer that won't fit is skipped, not truncated.
I drafted the default publisher agreement and insertion order, then negotiated changes for the first studio that signed.
